Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers + artifacts attached (see SBOM and process doc). High level:

1) SBOM: We produce an SPDX v2.2 SBOM for every production build delivered for private deployments. Each SBOM is signed with an RSA-4096 key and timestamped. The SBOM includes component name, version, package supplier, checksum (sha256), build environment ID, and applicable CVE references.

2) Offline patching: For air-gapped sites we produce an "offline patch bundle" (tar.gz) that contains: signed binaries, delta packages where applicable, an SPDX SBOM for the bundle, and a detached signature. Verification steps: verify signature using the public key we provide -> verify bundle checksum -> run dry-run installer validating preflight checks. The installer supports a verification-only mode to validate before applying.

3) Third-party control: We maintain a mirrored internal registry for all container images used in private deployments and publish image-level SBOM entries. We run CVE scans at build time and publish a remediation status per component. For high-risk CVEs we provide backported patches as part of the offline bundle.

4) Emergency fixes: Our standard SLA for critical security patches to dedicated/private customers is 72 hours to produce a signed emergency bundle; typical rollback is via the same offline bundle with versioned manifests and an automated rollback script. For very complex changes we do a canary apply on a test cluster before customer rollout — we can include a canary bundle with the delivery.

5) Customer registries & key rotation: We support customer-hosted registries and provide scripts to mirror artifacts into a private registry. Key rotation is supported via an outlined process in the attached install doc; we also support HSM-based key storage on request.

Attachments: SBOM_Redwood_v1.4.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); airgap-update-process.md (Markdown, 24KB)

Marta — quick technical clarifications following Kimberly's summary:

- Signed SBOM: we sign the SPDX JSON using RSA-4096 and include a SHA-256 digest of the build artifact. If you require PGP signatures instead we can provide that in parallel.
- Bundle format: offline patch bundles are tar.gz archives with a top-level manifest.json that lists artifacts, semantic versions, and the signature file name (manifest.sig). The manifest includes a per-file sha256.
- Verification: the verification tool exits non-zero on mismatch and offers a --rebuild-checksums mode for reproducibility checks.
- Registry mirroring: our mirroring scripts push images to a customer-provided registry and record the mirror mapping in the SBOM metadata. We support both docker registry v2 and OCI registries.

I can attach a sample manifest and a short example of the verification log if that helps.
